segments.text: Yes, I'm very well too, thank you. Today, Neil, in this conversation, we're talking about moving house. So when was the last time you moved house?

segments.text: Oh, wow. And why did you move to where you live now?

segments.text: Because my family was getting bigger. More children need more space. So we moved to somewhere bigger and further out of London. How about you?

segments.text: I rent my flat and the place I was living before, the owners of the place wanted to sell the house.

segments.text: It has good transport links and yeah it was a good a good decision

segments.text: And how was the move itself

segments.text: I'm a bit of a minimalist.

segments.text: The reason is because I moved country,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: so I just didn't really have many things to bring back to the UK.

segments.text: It was the opposite of that.

segments.text: Oh, no.

segments.text: We had a removal van and some removal men

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: who came and packed everything up in boxes

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: to make sure that things were easy to carry into the van

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and also that they didn't get damaged.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And then they drove all of our stuff to my new house.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.text: Did you have any fragile bits?

segments.text: So fragile means that it's easy to break, not very strong plates and things.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Did you have?

segments.text: Yes, those things had to be wrapped and protected.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Otherwise, they would break.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes.

segments.text: And did you have to move furniture as well?

segments.text: Yeah, we had to move sofas and cupboards and wardrobes and heavy things like that.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.text: Does sound different to my experience, doesn't it?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I didn't have any furniture to take.

segments.text: Do you find moving house exciting Scary How do you feel about moving house

segments.text: I think it both It exciting and scary It exciting because this is going to be your new life

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: or where your new life will happen.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But it's also scary because you don't know what that's going to be like.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You don't know what your neighbours are going to be like.

segments.text: That's very true.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You don't know what your new friends are going to be like.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So there's lots of things that you don't know.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And that's scary, but also exciting.

segments.text: Yeah, a lot of uncertainty for sure.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah, I think it can depend.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It depends if you're moving somewhere better or worse.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But yeah, I was quite excited when I moved because I knew that my new flat had a nice outdoor terrace.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: As I said, we were close to parks and stuff.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I was excited.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Georgie, if you are planning a move, what do you need to do to prepare?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, you need to do things like setting up Wi-Fi in the new house, other bills like electricity and heating, gas.

segments.speaker: Georgie

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: You need to plan what you're going to take.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So when you move, it's a really good time to look at all of your possessions and think, what do I need?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Maybe I can get rid of stuff.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So throw stuff away.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Have you got any other ideas What else can you do to prepare for a move

segments.text: You can hire a removal company or van if you doing it yourself

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you need to transport your stuff to your new house

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and you can't just use a taxi.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Sounds like a lot of work.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I don't want to move anytime soon.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, me neither.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No.

segments.text: OK, let's recap the language we heard during the conversation.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We heard possessions, which are the things that you own or have.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: For example, my phone and my clothes are my possessions.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We talked about removal vans.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: A removal van is a large vehicle that people put your possessions into to go from one home to another.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And the company is called a removals company or removals firm.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We heard packing and packing is where you put your own things into boxes

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: so that a removal firm can take them to your new home.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we heard fragile.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Fragile is an adjective which describes something that can break easily.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, glass. Glass is fragile.
